title: Isolation Hedgebox and Scaleback Policy — PRD Idea
content:
Summary:

This is an exploratory PRD describing a lightweight tenant isolation primitive ("hedgebox") combined with a configurable scaleback policy for Redwood Dedicated pools. The goal: provide predictable degradation semantics for noisy bursts, allow short-duration isolation for high-risk tenants, and enable automated, preemptive capacity hedging that minimizes evictions and SLA churn. This doc focuses on behavior, API surface, observability signals, and an ops-safe rollout plan.

Problem statement:

Dedicated pools must balance two competing pressures: stable latency for latency-sensitive tenants and efficient utilization to maximize revenue. Current approaches (hard preemption, tenant eviction, blunt throttle rules) either cause customer-visible failures or leave capacity underutilized. We need a middle path that: 
- absorbs short-lived noisy bursts without full eviction,
- gracefully degrades tenant fidelity when capacity is strained,
- surfaces clear accounting for burst costs, and
- gives operators rollbackable controls to contain failure modes.

Goals (success metrics):

- Reduce full eviction incidents by 50% for tenants experiencing transient microbursts (<= 2 minutes).
- Maintain P95 text-gen latency within SLO for premium lanes in >= 99% of evaluated stress tests.
- Limit steady-state cost overhead of hedgeboxes to < 3% on average across active pools.
- Provide clear billing/ledger entries for hedged capacity within the Console (token-level reconciliation).

Non-goals:

- This is not a replacement for long-term capacity planning or hard-limits for abusive customers.
- We are not building a new pricing model here; billing changes will be minimal and surfaced as annotations.

Concept: Hedgebox (high level)

A hedgebox is a temporary, bounded isolation envelope for a tenant or tenant group that can be created automatically or via API when heuristics detect risky burst behavior. A hedgebox contains:
- Softly-isolated compute (logical slices + cache fencing) for the tenant for a defined window (e.g., 30–180s).
- A scaleback profile that progressively reduces resource fidelity (quantization fallback, KV cache warming priority reduction, batch sizing changes, and optional response truncation) according to latency/cost rules.
- A small headroom buffer (pre-allocated ephemeral capacity) that absorbs the initial burst while rules ramp the scaleback.

Key attributes:

- duration_window: user-configurable length for the hedgebox (short by default).
- escalation_policy: how quickly fidelity is reduced and whether fallback models are used.
- cost_ledger_tag: a string tag to mark tokens/requests billed while in hedgebox.
- preemptive_threshold: signal threshold to open a hedgebox automatically (traffic gradient, token/sec spike, queue depth).

Behavioral guarantees:

- Hedgebox activation must be decisive and reversible: when opened, the tenant is routed into isolated slices; when closed, routing returns to normal.
- No hard evictions: if the hedgebox is full and pressure persists, escalation goes to soft throttling and then controlled eviction with advance notifications.
- Signals and timing are deterministic and logged for audit.

Scaleback profiles (examples)

- Profile: latency-preserved (slow cost cut) — favor maintaining low tail latency by increasing cost: reduce batching window? (opposite) — actually latency-preserved should reduce background work, maintain inference paths; steps: reduce batching aggressiveness, keep higher-priority kernels, shed low-priority logging.
- Profile: cost-preserved (fast cut) — aggressive token quantization fallback, move to cheaper model variant for non-critical endpoints, offer truncation or summarization to keep requests within tokens.
- Profile: fidelity-tiered — progressive model step-down: full model -> quantized variant -> small distilled variant -> truncated output with explicit confidence flag.

API/Config surface (proposal)

1) Tenant-side flags (Console/API):
- enable_hedgebox: bool (default: true for early adopters)
- hedging_window_secs: int
- scaleback_profile: string (latency_preserved | cost_preserved | fidelity_tiered | custom)
- preemption_grace_secs: int (how long to wait before escalation to eviction)

2) Activation endpoints for ops and automation:
- POST /dedicated/tenants/{id}/hedgebox/activate body:{"reason":string, "duration_secs":int, "profile":string} 
- POST /dedicated/tenants/{id}/hedgebox/deactivate
- GET /dedicated/tenants/{id}/hedgebox/status

3) Runtime flags for serving runtime:
- hedged=true|false (routing metadata)
- eviction_score=(0..1) (computed by autoscaler)

Autoscaling integration

- Hedgeboxes work with the predictive autoscaler: when aggregate pool signals predict a short-term spike, the autoscaler may open hedgeboxes proactively for selected tenants rather than expand the warm-pool.
- Hedgebox pre-warms a tiny ephemeral slot to avoid cold start penalties while scaleback ramps.
- Autoscaler must be aware of hedged capacity as a separate accounting bucket to avoid double-counting when scaling decisions are made.

Observability and telemetry

Required metrics (per tenant/hedgebox):
- hedgebox_open_events: timestamped events with reason and profile
- hedged_requests_count
- token_ledger_tagged_tokens
- p50/p95/p99 latencies pre/post hedging
- fidelity_level_over_time (simple enum timeline)
- eviction_attempts and soft-throttle seconds

Console/Alerting UX:
- Per-tenant timeline overlay showing hedgebox windows, scaleback steps, and billing tags.
- Alert rule templates: "Tenant opened N hedgeboxes in M minutes" and "Aggregate hedged capacity > X% of pool".

Operational playbook (runbook sketch)

- Automated path: heuristics start hedgebox (preemptive_threshold breached) -> scaleback profile applied -> monitor 2x sampling windows -> close if normalized or escalate to soft-throttle -> notify tenant via webhooks.
- Manual path: SRE can open/close hedgeboxes and choose a profile; system records operator and reason; runbook includes rollback steps and tenant-notify templates.
- Escalation: if hedgebox duration expires and pressure persists, system escalates to tenant-level quota capping and then, as last resort, eviction with documented owner signoff.

Billing & Economics

- Hedgebox incurs normal per-token billing, with ledger tags to identify hedged traffic. For early phases we will not charge an extra premium; ledger is for internal cost attribution and for future product decisions.
- Report in Console: monthly hedged-token volume and estimated incremental cost.

Risk analysis and mitigations

- Risk: Hedgeboxes could be abused to mask cheating/abuse. Mitigation: integrate abuse detector signals to block hedging auto-open for flagged tenants.
- Risk: Complexity in autoscaler accounting. Mitigation: treat hedged capacity as a first-class capacity dimension and add unit tests + simulation harness.
- Risk: Tenant surprise/visibility. Mitigation: UI indicators, webhook notifications, and an opt-out flag for customers who prefer hard limits.

Rollout plan (phases)

- Phase 0 (experiment): Build internal simulation, run against historical traffic to tune thresholds. (4 weeks)
- Phase 1 (private alpha): Enable for small set of low-risk tenants and internal Redwood teams; SRE manual control. (6 weeks)
- Phase 2 (beta): Tenant-allowed feature, exposed in Console with default on for new tenants; telemetry enabled. (8 weeks)
- Phase 3 (GA): Public docs, SLA implications clarified, integrate billing ledger into reports. (12 weeks)

Open questions / items for follow-up

- Should hedged requests be discounted (to encourage use) or flagged as surcharge?
- Precise ordering of scaleback steps for different model topologies (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder workloads).
- How to present fidelity drop explanations to end-users of tenant apps (transparency vs UX confusion).

Appendix: quick scenarios

- Microburst (background indexing job floods requests for 90s): Hedgebox opens automatically, moves tenant to quantized kernel path with small pre-warmed ephemeral slot, backend finishes job without eviction, hedgebox closes.
- Sustained burst (noisy neighbor persists): Hedgebox opens, scaleback moves to distilled variant, after grace period operator notified and quota cap applied if pressure persists.

Next steps:

- Sync with Serving Runtime (Marina, Ravi) to validate per-shard isolation feasibility.
- Prototype autoscaler accounting stub and simulated event load with SRE.
- Draft Console UX mock for ledger and timeline view.

Notes:

This doc is intentionally an idea-stage PRD — seeking feedback on the hedging primitive and scaleback tradeoffs. Focus feedback requests: what must be enforced by runtime vs what can live in the orchestration layer; thresholds we should standardize; and early telemetry schemas.
